diagnosis: HBV calibrated with DDS (NSE objective) over 1971-10 to 1997-12 (1970-71 warm-up; initial soil moisture set near equilibrium, 250 mm). Full-period NSE 0.853, KGE 0.77, r 0.93. Split-sample check (calibrate 1971-1986, validate 1987-1997) gave validation NSE 0.861, so the NSE-optimal structure transfers well; a KGE-calibrated alternative had near-zero bias but lower validation NSE (0.834), so the NSE set was kept. Parameters: FC ~284 mm, LP 0.94, BETA 4.5, K0 0.59, K1 0.30, K2 0.086, UZL 3.9, PERC 1.37, MAXBAS 3.8; snow parameters are irrelevant (≈1% snow). Weaknesses: systematic overestimation of runoff volume (~14% PBIAS), likely from unrepresented losses or interbasin groundwater exchange in the chalk/limestone aquifer parts, and summer recession/low flows plus slow baseflow from the permeable part of the catchment are captured only approximately with the single fast-ish lower store. Peak timing and winter high flows from the clay-dominated area are well reproduced. Confidence: moderate-high in response/soil parameters (stable across seeds and sub-periods); the volume bias is a structural trade-off that NSE accepts.
